questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was close by and I felt that the academic level were on par with the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. I got an exchange email with all the sufficient information for the exchange period.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Emails about the introduction week and all the information regarding the locations and such.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was in a housing lottery and was lucky enough to get student accomendation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be fine if you're lucky in staying at a socially charged place

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: quite difficult to navigate in how to sign up for the courses correctly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course catalogue was not very intuitive. You had to have 4-5 different tabs open with so much different information.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I figured it out in the end, but it could have been much smoother.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Good luck. It can be very overwhelming at first, so take your time and make sure to keep a cool head.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was way to condensed in the way the courses worked. The courses were only for either 8 or 4 weeks with exams, so it can be, for some, a bit to superficial.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As the courses were so intens it can be difficult to adapt from the way classes work at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The same, but again, it was super boiled down and very not in depth.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Media Culture
Cultural Data Analysis
The Power of Persuasion: Argumentation and Rhetoric in the Information Age I
Media culture in transformation
Philosophy, Ethics & AI

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Cultural Data analysis and Philosophy, Ethics & AI were very interesting and up to date on the world situation.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Everything is expensive. If you're social and want to go out for drinks with friends, be aware of the costs of everything attached to that. Museums are expensive as well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Drinks, Food, museums, attractions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a group chat that was quite active with different activities being organised pretty much every week.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do the intro week. I meet my friend group during the time and primarily hung out with them during the mobility.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out with friends. During the holidays as it is so close to Denmark, go home and hangout with your family and friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Basically no difference in how people are from Denmark. They are nicer and more helpful though.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just do everything you can to get out there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It's very similar to Denmark, but again, people are a lot more open and kind.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get out there and socialise. If you go by yourself as i did, push yourself you do the social events.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some of the exams are different than the one at UCPH. I was quite surprised about the physical exams. It was a multiple choice exam for 2 hours with no tools.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Studying in a different country. It gave Me so much to think about, how it feels to live in a different country and studying abroad.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I want to say going back is the biggest challenge. You've been gone for what feels like a long time when you are there, but when you get home it feels weird. I feel like it's been a dream or an adventure and now I'm back again and nothing has really changed.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
